title: The Sample Pre-selection and Characterization Station at the SECUF: Instrumentation, Capabilities, and Representative Scientific Achievements
authors: Xu Chen, Tao Sun, Huifen Ren, Minjie Cui, Jun Luo, Shuai Zhang, Shaokui Su
abstract: The Synergetic Extreme Condition User Facility (SECUF) is a comprehensive, state-of-the-art user facility designed to provide integrated extreme physical conditions-including ultrahigh pressure, ultralow temperature, strong magnetic fields, and ultrafast optical fields-for frontier research in condensed matter physics and materials science. Within SECUF, the F2 Sample Pre-selection and Characterization Station plays a pivotal supporting role. Its mission is to provide comprehensive sample synthesis, processing, pre-screening, and characterization services to prepare high-quality specimens for subsequent experiments under extreme conditions. This paper details the specifications and performance of ten core instrument systems within these units. Furthermore, we highlight several breakthrough scientific achievements enabled by the F2 Station, encompassing the discovery of novel quantum spin supersolid states, pressure-induced high-temperature superconductivity in nickelates, giant anomalous Hall angles, and molecular water in lunar soil. We also outline ongoing technical developments that expand the station's capabilities, such as integrated high-pressure cells and self-built ancillary measurement systems.
summary: This paper details the advanced instrumentation capabilities of the F2 Sample Pre-selection and Characterization Station at SECUF. By integrating multiple extreme conditions—such as high pressure, low temperature, and strong magnetic fields—the facility allows for comprehensive characterization of novel quantum materials. The reported achievements underscore its role in discovering exotic states like high-Tc superconductivity under immense pressure.

method: A suite of advanced experimental techniques is utilized, combining electrical transport measurements (resistivity, heat capacity) with structural characterization (XRD, SEM) under extreme conditions like ultrahigh pressure and ultralow temperature.

important_parameters: Temperatures down to $<10$ mK; Magnetic fields up to $\pm 16$ T; Pressures up to 70 GPa.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the combination of extreme physical conditions can unlock novel quantum phases and material properties inaccessible under ambient conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comprehensive instrumentation overview, including PPMS, MPMS, DR, NMR, SCXRD, XRD, SEM, Raman, and FT-IR systems, alongside details of instrument upgrades like high-pressure cells.
paper_structure: The paper details the specifications of ten core instrument systems within the F2 Station. It then highlights several breakthrough scientific achievements enabled by these combined capabilities, such as superconductivity in nickelates and anomalous Hall effects.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science instrumentation, the reported discoveries (superconductivity, quantum spin states) are central to strongly correlated electron physics, which often involves complex many-body interactions relevant to theoretical modeling.
